title: Prompt, model and seed effects
outcome: Analyze a crossed prompt/model/seed experiment and distinguish decoding variability from independent task evidence.

exercises.title: Inspect each prompt
exercises.task: Calculate candidate minus baseline under each prompt.
exercises.hint: Average seeds before comparing aligned cells.
exercises.answer: An overall favorable result does not imply improvement under every configuration.

exercises.title: Check reconstruction
exercises.task: Recombine grand mean, model, prompt and interaction terms.
exercises.expected: Every observed cell is recovered within floating tolerance.
exercises.hint: Broadcast model effects down rows and prompt effects across columns.
exercises.answer: This algebraic identity is a useful implementation check, independent of any inferential assumptions.

exercises.title: Change the prompt target
exercises.task: Put all deployment weight on the first prompt.
exercises.hint: The target distribution is part of the estimand.
exercises.answer: A fixed-prompt deployment needs evidence for that prompt, not an attractive average over unused alternatives.

exercises.title: Equalize selection budgets
exercises.task: Select the best prompt separately for both models on development data.
exercises.hint: Apply the same procedure to both candidates.
exercises.answer: A comparison of selection procedures differs from a comparison of one selected system with an untuned mean; final assessment must still be independent.

exercises.title: Count seed replication
exercises.task: Compute variance for baseline/prompt 1 across its three authored seeds.
exercises.hint: Use `ddof=1` for this descriptive sample calculation.
exercises.answer: This describes the three constructed seed scores. It does not quantify variation across an unseen population of task families.

exercises.title: Validate axes
exercises.task: Provide only a two-dimensional matrix to the helper.
exercises.hint: Every dimension must retain its scientific meaning.
exercises.answer: Silently averaging an unidentified axis can mix model, prompt and replication factors and invalidate the comparison.
